# OpenWorkProof

> OpenWorkProof helps developers check what an AI agent was authorized to do, what actions were recorded, and what the available evidence supports. It provides signed work records, local MCP tools and offline bundle verification.

## Current release

OpenWorkProof 1.6.1 exposes 32 local stdio MCP tools. The Python package requires Python 3.10 or newer. The package also includes a separately enabled experimental Codex Guard and an experimental SOC reference CLI. Publication, installation, protection, verification and human acceptance are separate facts.

## Start with a concrete task

- Review supplied Slips alerts: the three reference SOC tools return source-window cases and a signed evidence bundle. Investigation uses a deterministic stub and actions are simulated; there is no real host remediation. A synthetic sample is available for an installation check.
- Recheck an exported bundle: verify signatures and evidence links within the selected verifier's stated scope. SOC verification returns UNKNOWN without separately obtained expected public keys and witnessed checkpoints. Copying a bundle's own trust materials is only an internal consistency demonstration.
- Integrate Agent work records: use Core schemas, signed requests, receipts, ledger checks and delivery packages in an existing workflow. A verification result does not replace a person's acceptance decision or prove payment.
- Restrict a Codex preview task: install and explicitly enable Guard for its supported local text-editing scope, then run its live probe and doctor. Initial live checks used macOS, Python 3.12 and Codex CLI 0.147.0. Generic MCP installation does not enable Guard or protect other Agent tool calls.

## Connect MCP

Use a stdio-capable local MCP client to launch `uvx --from openworkproof==1.6.1 owp-mcp`. The MCP client manages this process. There is no hosted remote endpoint or API key in this setup. `owp` is the separate CLI, not the stdio server.

The optional `openworkproof-soc-review` Agent Skill is installable with `npx skills add dengyier/OpenWorkProof --skill openworkproof-soc-review`. The Skill supplies instructions; it does not configure MCP or grant host permissions.

- [中文说明](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/blob/main/README_zh-CN.md): Complete Chinese counterpart to the English README.

- [SOC reference workflow](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/blob/main/docs/integrations/soc-reference.md): Supplied-alert review, trust input formats and verification limits.
- [Codex Guard onboarding](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/blob/main/docs/integrations/agent-guard-onboarding.md): Separate scope review, activation, probe, doctor and guarded execution.
- [SOC Review Skill](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/blob/main/skills/openworkproof-soc-review/SKILL.md): Instructions for using the three reference SOC MCP tools.
- [Offline verification](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/blob/main/docs/offline-verification.md): Core signed evidence and acceptance workflows.
- [Protocol schemas](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/tree/main/specs): Authoritative schema sources.
- [Detailed project records, English](https://github.com/dengyier/OpenWorkProof/blob/main/docs/reference/project-overview-en.md): Preserved protocol, community and historical validation details.
